messages.text: Mahomes makes winning return as Chiefs storm past Broncos

metadata.summary: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night.
metadata.content: Patrick Mahomes returns from knee injury as Kansas City Chiefs storm past Denver Broncos | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Patrick Mahomes returns from knee injury as Kansas City Chiefs storm past Denver Broncos Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker stars on his Kansas City Chiefs debut with the most rushing yards by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles in 2012, posting 173 and two touchdowns; Walker signed with the Chiefs in free agency after guiding the Seattle Seahawks to Super Bowl glory Tuesday 15 September 2026 08:44, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Denver Broncos at the Kansas City Chiefs in the NFL Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night. Mahomes did not appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, as he threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as AFC West division champions. Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Kimi Antonelli must remain wary about the potential of unexpected "black swan events" derailing his championship bid despite the Italian driver's large points lead. Antonelli's back-to-back wins in Monza and Madrid have increased his championship advantage over team-mate George Russell to 81 points with a scheduled nine rounds remaining. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, third and fourth in the standings respectively, are now over 100 points behind.
